reading.rtitle: Board pack -- the page that goes out on the Friday before
paras: Headline. Coverage in the workshop segment is at nineteen per cent against a target of twenty-two, and the recommendation on the table has not changed: the budget should stay where it is, and we must not buy the gap with a discount. The takeaway, if you remember nothing else from this page, is that we are three points behind and we are behind on purpose.

What happened. We launched the coverage programme in March and the first quarter on quarter movement was slower than the projection, because the first visit to a new workshop is the expensive one and we underestimated how many visits it takes. What is happening now. The rollout is running about a week behind, the bottleneck is the label supplier, and we are splitting that order from Thursday. Two regions are ahead of plan and the south is not.

What comes next, and what we need. We are going to hold the price through the fiscal year and we are not going to run the trade fair. The projection for January is a range rather than a single number, between twenty-two and twenty-five per cent, because the second wave of visits has not started yet. From this board we have to have the budget signed before the fifteenth. We would like a second field team and we do not have to have it this year. Everything on this page is open to discussion except one line, and it is the discount.

listenings.text: Good morning. Three points and one decision, and I plan to be finished in ten minutes. Here is the headline first, because I would rather you heard it from me. Coverage is at nineteen against a target of twenty-two. We are three points behind, and we are behind on purpose. Point one, what happened. We launched in March and the first quarter on quarter movement was slower than the projection, because the first visit to a new workshop is the expensive one and we underestimated the number of visits. Point two, where we are today. The rollout is running a week behind, the bottleneck is the label supplier, and we are splitting that order from Thursday. Point three, and this is the one I want to spend longer on. We are going to hold the price through the fiscal year, and the January projection is a range rather than a number. The decision I need from this board today is the budget, and the deadline is the fifteenth.

After twenty years of sitting on boards I can tell you what separates the presentations we remember from the ones we do not, and it has almost nothing to do with the numbers. The ones we remember have a headline. One sentence, at the top, that survives the meeting. If the only thing a board member repeats in the corridor afterwards is your headline, you have done the job, and if they repeat something you said by accident, you have not. The second thing is a range. Anybody who gives me a single number for a period that has not happened yet is either lucky or is guessing, and I would much rather be told between twenty-two and twenty-five than be told twenty-three and find out in February that it was decoration. And the third, which is rarer than it should be, is somebody who flags the bad news themselves, early, in their own words. A board can work with a problem it heard about in October. It cannot work with the same problem in February.
